subject: Service credit schedule & SLA exception request — ConnorTech onboarding
messages:
From: Simon Connor <simon.connor@connortech.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template review / onboarding ask

Karthik / Laura —

Thanks for taking time yesterday. As we discussed in the call, ConnorTech will be onboarding our first batch of production traffic the week of May 3rd. We appreciate the standard 99.9% availability target in the template, but given the expected ramp (bursting to 3x baseline during ingestion windows) we need two things clarified before signatures: (1) a temporary exception window for onboarding where the availability tolerance widens modestly, and (2) a clearly defined monthly billing offset (service credit) formula if performance dips beyond the standard band.

I attached our internal MOPs for the onboarding spike and a one-page ask. High-level: we are comfortable with the 99.9% target after a 60‑day stabilization; for the first 30 days we need a carveout that limits our financial exposure. Can you propose wording/limits that align with Redwood policy?

Simon
Simon Connor
VP Engineering, ConnorTech
simon.connor@connortech.com
+1 415-555-0123

---
Attachment: CONNORTECH_ONBOARDING_MOP.pdf (referenced)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Simon Connor <simon.connor@connortech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service credit schedule & SLA exception request — ConnorTech onboarding

Simon —

Thanks for the context and the MOP. We can accommodate an onboarding exception but want to balance predictability and operational risk. Proposed approach (summary):

• Temporary onboarding carveout: a 30‑day onboarding window starting at first production cutover where the availability target is relaxed to 99.5% for the purposes of credit calculation only (not a permanent SLA change).
• Monthly billing offset (service credit) formula during that window: credits capped at 15% of monthly invoice for the onboarding month; credits prorated by the percentage shortfall below 99.5% using a linear scale where 0.1% shortfall → 2% credit, 0.5% shortfall → 10% credit, >1.0% shortfall triggers a max 15% credit.
• Monitoring & mitigation obligations: ConnorTech to enable our extended telemetry hooks for the 30‑day window (token-level logging for onboarding traces) and Redwood to commit to daily syncs during any >0.3% shortfall event.

I attached a redline to the standard SLA with the exact copy we would propose for your legal/procurement review (connortech_sla_redline_v1.pdf). Two ask items from our side: can you confirm the exact start date for the cutover so we can time the 30‑day window, and confirm whether your billing team will accept a credit cap applied as an invoice-level offset (preferred) or a separate credit memo.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0218

Attachment: connortech_sla_redline_v1.pdf

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ConnorTech onboarding — credit cap and ops guardrails

Karthik — quick internal note before we send the redline back. Keeping this in the thread for context.

I reviewed your draft and I'm supportive of a 30‑day onboarding carveout, but recommend we: 1) tighten the shortfall trigger thresholds so we don't have frequent daily syncs for tiny blips, and 2) add an absolute dollar cap fallback (e.g., no more than $25k in credits in the onboarding month) to protect against outsized credits if the customer invoice is very large.

Proposed adjustments to your formula:
• Trigger for daily ops sync: only if shortfall >0.3% (keep your text).
• Credit linear scale: 0.1% shortfall → 1.5% credit; 0.5% → 8% credit; >1.0% → capped at the lesser of 15% or $25k.
• Add a requirement that ConnorTech must have configured our recommended traffic shaping for the initial 30 days (we'll share a checklist). If they don't, onboarding exception is voided and standard SLA applies immediately.

Marissa — looping you for SRE confirmation on telemetry hooks and to confirm the checklist we should share. If you sign off, I'll send the redline back to Simon with the updated language and the DocuSign link.

Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service credit schedule & SLA exception request — ConnorTech onboarding

Laura / Karthik —

Thanks — that approach is reasonable and gives us the predictability procurement needs. A few quick clarifications from my side before we sign:

1) The $25k absolute cap is acceptable as long as the invoice offset is applied as a credit on the May invoice. We prefer invoice-level offset.
2) We can confirm the cutover window: planned start May 4th at 03:00 UTC. Please mark the 30‑day carveout May 4 → June 3.
3) For the traffic-shaping checklist we can commit to the items that don't require code changes; anything that requires a feature flag toggle we may need help from Redwood SREs. Can Marissa confirm SRE availability for a short runbook and one exec‑level contact for escalations?

If you can update the redline to include the $25k cap language and the start date, we're ready to route for signature. We'll sign via DocuSign once we have the final PDF (please add the HubSpot deal link in the cover email).

Simon
